finalText:
**Bug: intermediate rounding in `engine.js`, not coupon stacking.**

`computeTotal` rounded USD subtotal to 2 decimals after *each* coupon step (old lines 24, 27), then converted to target currency. Contract (and test reference) says round **once**, at end, in target currency's decimals.

Why it look like promo-stacking bug: only percent coupons make sub-cent USD values. `19.98 * 0.9 = 17.982`. Flat coupon subtract whole-cent amount from whole-cent subtotal — no residue, so flat-only carts always fine.

Why "most look fine": premature round throws away max half cent USD, then FX rate multiply it. Error only visible when it push target amount across rounding boundary.

- GBP, SAVE10PCT, 2x$9.99: exact `17.982 * 0.78 = 14.02596` → **14.03**. Old: `17.98 * 0.78 = 14.0244` → 14.02.
- EUR same cart: both paths land 16.18. Passes. Look fine.
- JPY, zero-decimal, rate 149: half-cent USD ≈ 0.75 yen, so 2x$10.04 gave 2692 instead of **2693**.

Failure spread: 10 of 40 — GBP and CAD (percent, both baskets), JPY (percent, $10.04 basket). USD and EUR never trip. Stacked `SAVE10PCT,FLAT5` fails in exactly same cells as `SAVE10PCT` alone — flat add nothing, it was percent all along.

Fix: drop both intermediate `round` calls, keep single `round(target, decimalsFor(order.currency))` at end. 40/40 pass.

Aside, unrelated, untested: no clamp at zero — `FLAT15` on cart under $15 returns negative total.
